source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.claim: The deterministic directed three-cycle has uniform invariant law, violates detailed balance, and its reverse kernel traverses the cycle in the opposite direction.
source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.concrete_content: Draw states 0, 1, 2 on a triangle. Use solid clockwise arrows labeled p(i,i+1)=1 and dashed counterclockwise arrows labeled p*(i,i−1)=1; note π(i)=1/3 at each vertex. Include a compact edge check at 0→1 showing π(0)p(0,1)=1/3 while π(1)p(1,0)=0. The diagram must distinguish invariant mass labels from transition directions and must not imply detailed balance.
source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.likelihood: High: the complete counterexample is a three-state directed graph, and the reversal is a direct visual comparison of opposite edge directions.
